# truefoundry_secret_group (Resource)

Manages a TrueFoundry secret group (`secret-group` manifest) — the named bucket that individual secrets live in, backed by a secret store such as a `truefoundry_system_secret_store` or a `truefoundry_hashicorp_account`. Secrets in the group are referenced as `tfy-secret://…` from every credential attribute this provider exposes.

**The group resource manages only the group.** Secrets in it are created either with `truefoundry_secret` (the value is then stored in the Terraform state) or out of band, which keeps secret material out of the state — and means Terraform cannot recreate them. **Destroying or renaming a group deletes every secret it holds**, so put `lifecycle { prevent_destroy = true }` on groups backing live credentials.

Import an existing group by its name: `terraform import truefoundry_secret_group.example system`.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# The secret store the group is backed by. A truefoundry_hashicorp_account
# works the same way.
resource "truefoundry_system_secret_store" "system" {
  name = "system-secret-store"

  secret_stores = [
    { name = "system-secret-store" },
  ]
}

# The group itself. Secrets inside it are created with truefoundry_secret
# (the value is then stored in the Terraform state) or out of band — through
# the TrueFoundry UI or API — which keeps secret material out of the state.
resource "truefoundry_secret_group" "system" {
  name            = "system"
  integration_fqn = "${truefoundry_system_secret_store.system.fqn}:secret-store:system-secret-store"

  # Destroying or renaming the group deletes every secret in it, and Terraform
  # cannot recreate them. Guard groups that back live credentials.
  lifecycle {
    prevent_destroy = true
  }
}

# Secrets in the group are referenced from any credential attribute by their
# FQN, <tenant>:<group>:<secret>:
#
#   resource "truefoundry_provider_account" "openai" {
#     # ...
#     api_key = "tfy-secret://${truefoundry_secret_group.system.fqn}:openai-api-key"
#   }
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `integration_fqn` (String) FQN of the secret store integration backing the group, e.g. of a `truefoundry_system_secret_store`: my-tenant:truefoundry:system-secret-store:secret-store:system-secret-store. A group cannot be moved between stores — the control plane rejects the change rather than silently migrating the secrets.
- `name` (String) Name of the secret group (5-50 characters; must start with a lowercase letter, end with a letter or digit, and contain only lowercase letters, digits and hyphens, no consecutive hyphens), unique within the tenant. **Changing it replaces the group, which deletes every secret stored in it** — the secrets are created out of band and Terraform cannot recreate them.

### Optional

- `collaborators` (Attributes Set, Deprecated) Subjects with a role on this secret group; use `truefoundry_role_binding` instead. Unset leaves the grants on the control plane untouched (and they are not tracked); an empty set clears them, which is only accepted until 15 Nov 2026. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--collaborators))

### Read-Only

- `fqn` (String) Fully qualified name of the group, `<tenant>:<name>`. Secrets in it are addressed as `<tenant>:<name>:<secret>`.
- `id` (String) Control plane ID of the secret group.

<a id="nestedatt--collaborators"></a>
### Nested Schema for `collaborators`

Required:

- `role_id` (String) Role to assign, e.g. secret-group-admin, secret-group-manager, secret-group-editor, secret-group-access, or secret-group-viewer.
- `subject` (String) Subject FQN, e.g. user:jane@example.com or team:everyone.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Secret groups are imported by their name (not their FQN).
terraform import truefoundry_secret_group.system system
```
